name: A Saint for Me — House Style v1
summary: Contemporary devotional art: surrealist, Afrofuturist hand-cut and torn paper collage, built from vintage printed matter, crystals, abstract stained glass and celestial imagery, in vibrant pink, turquoise, orange, coral and peach.

palette.rules: Saturated, joyful color against either warm aged paper or deep night grounds. Pink and turquoise are the signature pairing. Gold is used sparingly as leaf or seams, never as a glowing haze.

techniques: hand-cut paper collage with visible scissor edges
torn paper edges with white deckled fibers showing
layered cut-outs casting soft, real paper shadows
vintage halftone printing and misregistered risograph color
archival ephemera: botanical engravings, star charts, ledger paper, postage-stamp perforations, old hymnal page textures (no legible words)
abstract stained-glass segmentation with dark lead lines
faceted crystals and gemstones as luminous solid forms
gold-leaf seams in the manner of kintsugi

preferences: bold central symbol with generous negative space
asymmetric balance, slightly tilted cut-out layers
depth built from physical layering rather than digital blur
an arch, window or halo shape used as a framing device
one clear focal point readable at phone size

archetypes.description: a single central emblem inside a large stained-glass halo, radiating cut-paper rays
a tall Gothic-arch window cut from paper, opening onto a surreal celestial landscape
concentric orbits and planetary rings circling a central crystal or figure
a vertical tower of collaged layers rising from earth strata toward stars
two halves in conversation, a seam or thread joining contrasting fields
a mandala-like rose window of radial stained-glass petals and gems
layered torn-paper horizons like geological strata under a vast sky
scattered cut-out elements connected by fine thread like a star chart
an off-center collaged profile silhouette filled with a cosmos, flowers or crystals
three vertical panels like a contemporary altarpiece, each a variation on the theme

textures: visible paper fiber at torn edges

universal: crescent moons, eight-pointed stars, planetary rings
afrocentric: Black women and men as dignified, regal collage silhouettes or portraits
headwraps, braids and natural hair rendered as cut-paper shapes
geometric patterns inspired by West African textiles (mudcloth, strip-woven cloth)
cowrie shells, indigo dye patterns, sun disks
Afrofuturist celestial adornment: crowns of stars, orbiting jewels
sacred: halos as stained-glass rings, not glowing blur
a simple Latin cross or Chi-Rho used sparingly and accurately
a dove for the Holy Spirit
the Sacred Heart as a flaming heart with a small cross (only when relevant)
lilies, roses and palms as traditional attributes

lighting.atmosphere: luminous through color, not glow: light comes from saturated hues, gemstone facets and stained glass, with gentle paper shadows
lighting.avoid: lens flares, god rays, glowing haze, bloom effects

typography.inImage: no text, letters, numerals or pseudo-writing in the generated image
typography.onCards: high-contrast serif display (Fraunces) for titles; prayer set in italic serif; small caps for labels; generous margins

sacredIconographyRules: Do not depict Jesus, Mary or specific saints as photorealistic portraits.
When a sacred person appears, use a symbolic, abstracted collage treatment with correct traditional attributes.
Use only accurate Christian symbols; never invent pseudo-religious symbols or add occult or esoteric signs.
No halos on figures representing the user; halos belong to sacred figures only.
No angels depicted as cherubs or generic winged women.
Saint portraits are artistic interpretations, not historical likenesses.
avoid: glowing heavenly backgrounds, sunbeams through clouds
overly literal depictions of the user's situation
money, coins, banknotes or price tags
photorealism, 3D render look, plastic CGI sheen
